# M14 independent protocol and expected outcomes

Frozen before implementation or product execution. The twelve local diagnostic
references retain all six strata in both calibration and held-out roles; their
six-per-role size is explicitly inadequate for the predeclared sixty-per-role
qualification gate. Source placeholders represent unavailable authorized external
cohort snapshots. Native helpers may bind a named local row to an actual snapshot
before inference, while preserving every expected label and handling outcome.
A future larger cohort requires a new frozen protocol before its observations.

The selected-option probability is a backend-specific diagnostic statistic, not
universal calibrated confidence. The predeclared threshold procedure chooses the
lowest calibration candidate meeting its numeric gate, then evaluates the held-out
split without retuning. A one-sided 95% Wilson bound, with the fixed z value in the
protocol, constrains wrong routing. Unavailable and malformed rows remain in total
and handling denominators. No exclusion, duplicate row, post-measurement target
change, fixture relabeling, or synthetic model-quality claim is authorized.

The expanded numeric test cohort repeats the independently specified handling
patterns under distinct source hashes to verify arithmetic only. It carries no
canonical inference receipts and cannot be published as live qualification.
All route outcomes in native checks are existing durable manual-work requests.

## Frozen metric denominators

Each role denominator is every enrolled case in that role. Wrong-route rate uses
all routed cases as its denominator; the Wilson bound uses the same routed count.
Incorrect-review rate uses every enrolled role case, and route coverage is routed
cases divided by every enrolled role case. Missing, unavailable and malformed
observations stay in that role denominator and are also reported separately.
Calibrating does not tune on held-out outcomes. Two additional independent Wilson
constants are 0/30 = 0.08272430812509929 and 1/30 = 0.136404142151817; the latter
fails the 0.10 uncertainty gate while passing the 0.05 point-rate gate. These
definitions and fault oracles were clarified by independent review before any
implementation output or native execution; no numeric threshold changed.
